placements.why: The content describes a mandated organizational onboarding procedure — a structured process governing how new hires are integrated, established through supersession of a prior artifact. This names an organizational category the graph's strata does not yet hold, and future envelopes describing institutional routines, process mandates, and organizational procedures will accumulate here.
placements.title: Organizational practice and process
placements.frame: What mandated procedures, process authorities, and institutional routines shape how work is structured and integrated?

placements.title: From ad-hoc wiki to mandated checklist
placements.frame: How does an onboarding process become the operative authority, and what does its supersession of prior practice establish about institutional legitimacy?
placements.why: Both segments perform the legitimation of the Pallasine checklist as the operative onboarding authority: src-1 states the universal first-week mandate (accounts, pairing rotation, shadow shift) as settled practice, performing a ratified decision; src-2 grounds that authority in the supersession of the old wiki page last quarter, supplying the historical claim that completes the legitimation arc. The theme — how a structured process becomes authoritative through replacement of a predecessor — is a subject future envelopes will keep feeding, not a one-time fact.
